issues.description: The problem statement and the template define/addParent(Person person, Person parent) (child first, parent second). In the solution, the addParent method's parameter order is reversed (addParent(Person parent, Person person)), which contradicts the intended signature and the way tests in the solution call the method. This parameter-order mismatch is structural and will confuse students about the correct argument order and expected semantics of addParent.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the addParent method signature in the solution match the intended signature and the template: public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent). Adjust parameter names and implementation accordingly so the first parameter represents the child (person) and the second the parent. Ensure any calls (tests) use the same ordering.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect PersonService.addParent to take the target person (child) as the first parameter and the parent as the second (addParent(Person person, Person parent)). In the solution, the addParent method declares its parameters in the opposite order/names (addParent(Person parent, Person person)). PersonResource (both template and solution) calls addParent(person, persistedParent) (child then parent). This mismatch in parameter naming/order between the solution implementation and the problem/template creates confusion about which argument represents the child vs. the parent and may lead students to misunderstand the intended API and behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution's PersonService.addParent signature and parameter names with the problem statement and template: declare addParent(Person person, Person parent) (child first, parent second) and use these parameter names in the implementation. Ensure all call sites (PersonResource, tests) pass arguments in the same order (child, parent).
